subject: Hospitality Studies
source: November 2026 Hospitality Studies Paper 1 study guide (topics, key facts, common mistakes and exam tips from the 2021-2025 November papers)
overview: Hospitality Studies has one Grade 12 theory paper: 200 marks, 3 hours, 6 compulsory questions, no choice. Question 1 (40 marks) is short questions from all six topics: multiple choice, matching columns, fill-in terms and select/reorder items. The order of Questions 2-6 is fixed: Q2 Kitchen and Restaurant Operations plus Hygiene, Safety and Security (20); Q3-Q4 Nutrition and Menu Planning plus Food Commodities (80 combined); Q5 Sectors and Careers (30); Q6 Food and Beverage Service (30). No essays: the longest answers are 6-8 marks built from three or four facts. Almost every question from Q2 is built on a scenario, menu, picture or advert. Marking: mostly 2 marks per well-explained fact, so a one-word answer to an 'explain' or 'discuss' question usually earns nothing. Only the first X answers asked for are marked, so lead with the strongest. 'Evaluate', 'judge', 'critique' and 'argue' questions give ONE mark for a stance (good/bad, suitable/unsuitable) before the reasons. Use exact terms. Costing calculations are marked step by step: formula, substitution and answer each earn marks.

tiers.title: Paper 1 topics, heaviest first (share of the topic marks over 2021-2025)

atomic_skills.title: Food commodities (30.8%)
atomic_skills.description: The biggest topic every year: meat, poultry and fish quality and cuts, pastry (puff, choux, shortcrust), preservation methods, gelatine and meringue desserts, product labels and food costing. Quality signs per meat type: colour, texture, smell and fat. Puff/flaky pastry has many thin layers from a cold-fat method (cold ingredients keep the fat solid, which makes it flaky); choux is piped, hollow inside and raised by steam; shortcrust is blind-baked for a pre-cooked filling. Canning: heat plus an airtight seal keeps oxygen out. Glazing/candying: repeated cooking in a concentrated sugar syrup. Freezing needs an airtight seal or freezer burn and dehydration follow. Costing, always in this order: Total cost = Food cost + Labour cost + Overhead cost; Selling price = Food cost ÷ Food cost %; Net profit = Selling price - Total cost.

error_signatures.description: Writing only the final number in a costing question: the formula, substitution and answer each earn their own mark

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Identify the exact commodity, cut, pastry or preservation method first. For identification questions write only the exact term the memo wants ('choux pastry', not 'pastry'). For preservation, name the method, then explain how it removes water, sugar-saturates or kills microbes.

atomic_skills.title: Food and beverage service (21.7%)
atomic_skills.description: Wine (types, labels, storage, pairing, service), cocktails and mocktails, table setting and cover-checking, service styles and handling difficult guests. Still/natural wine has nothing added during fermentation; sparkling wine has CO2 (via MCC, Charmat or carbonation); fortified wine has spirits added, which stops fermentation. Silver service: the waiter serves from a platter at the table. Plated: food arrives plated from the kitchen. Gueridon: prepared or finished at a trolley beside the table. Buffet: guests serve themselves. Liquor licence: on-consumption means drinking on the premises (needs guest toilets and food available); off-consumption means bought to drink elsewhere. No one under 18 may be served or employed to serve.

error_signatures.description: Describing only one side of a compare/differentiate question: both items need paired facts

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Name the service style or equipment first. Classify a wine, then give its label facts and serving temperature. For difficult-guest scenarios: a professional first response, then who to call in. 'Judge/evaluate' service questions want a stance word as the first mark.

atomic_skills.title: Nutrition and menu planning (18.4%)
atomic_skills.description: Finger food and hors d'oeuvre planning, special-diet menus, menu-writing rules and menu-planning principles. Vegan: no animal products. Lacto-ovo: also dairy and eggs. Pesco: also fish. Pollo: also poultry. Flexitarian: mostly plant-based with occasional meat. Hindu: no beef, often vegetarian. Muslim/Halal: no pork or alcohol, animals slaughtered a specific way. Jewish/Kosher: no pork or shellfish, no milk with meat, separate utensils. Menu-planning principles: variety of colour, texture, flavour, temperature and cooking method across courses; don't repeat the same main ingredient. Menu-writing questions check capitalisation, course names, spacing and the date.

error_signatures.description: Giving a general reason for a special-diet question instead of naming the specific ingredient in the specific dish ('the bacon in the bacon-stuffed mushrooms', not 'the mushrooms')

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: 'Evaluate the menu' is two questions: find what's wrong (repetition, no variety) and why it matters for the occasion (season, budget, guests). Check all five: colour, texture, flavour, temperature, cooking method.

atomic_skills.title: Sectors and careers (17.1%)
atomic_skills.description: Departments, job roles and responsibilities, marketing, entrepreneurship and business plans, and the industry's effect on the South African economy. Revenue-generating areas: rooms, restaurant/bar, spa, conference and function rooms (guests pay directly). Non-revenue: reception, housekeeping, laundry, maintenance, security, HR, finance. Marketing mix: Product, Place, Price, Promotion, People, sometimes Packaging/Presentation. Economic impact chain: business income, job creation, higher local income and living standards, the multiplier effect, higher GDP, more tax and foreign currency. Business plan order: description, goals, personnel and job descriptions, marketing, cash flow. A good advert has the company name, contact details, a short message, eye-catching design and error-free wording.

error_signatures.description: Naming a department when the question asks for an area (for example 'housekeeping department' instead of 'guest rooms' or 'laundry')

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Decide revenue vs non-revenue first. For job roles, name the department, then the specific duty. 'Evaluate the advert' wants a stance first, then features present or missing.

atomic_skills.title: Kitchen and restaurant operations (6.8%)
atomic_skills.description: Computerised stock and reservation systems, online purchasing and booking safety, and staff professionalism, ethics and customer care. Why computerise: fewer errors, stock deducted automatically, faster service, instant reservation confirmation, easier record-keeping. Online purchasing safety: check for https and a padlock, use a reputable reviewed supplier, use a card with a small limit, never save banking details on an unfamiliar site. Work ethics: punctuality, honesty, reliability, respect, teamwork. For stock control, name the specific information needed (product name, quantity, price, reorder level).

error_signatures.description: Describing what a staff member did wrong without naming the specific value broken (punctuality, reliability, honesty)

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: 'Impact on the business' questions link staff behaviour to guest satisfaction, then repeat business, then income and profit; lower profit is a safe final point.

atomic_skills.title: Hygiene, safety and security (5.1%)
atomic_skills.description: Disease outbreaks (cholera, gastroenteritis, hepatitis A, HIV/TB) used as scenarios for symptoms, transmission, prevention and workplace law. Most at risk: children, the elderly, malnourished people, people with weakened immune systems, people living with an infected person. Prevention: treated, boiled or bottled water; thorough handwashing with antiseptic soap; food cooked and stored properly; sick staff sent home; pest control. Most outbreaks trace back to contaminated water or unwashed hands. HIV-positive staff cannot be restricted from food-service work because of HIV status; it is illegal to discriminate. Only an additional infection, like diarrhoea or hepatitis, is grounds for exclusion.

error_signatures.description: Assuming HIV-positive staff should be sent home or restricted, which is factually and legally wrong unless another infectious condition is present

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Prevention questions are list questions: write short, separate, nameable actions, not one general sentence about 'being hygienic'.
